rules.title: Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO) – Allowed Reasons for Eviction
rules.requirement: A landlord may only evict a tenant for specific at-fault reasons (failure to pay rent, breach of lease, nuisance, illegal use, failure to renew similar lease, denial of access, or unapproved subtenant) or no-fault reasons (owner or family move-in, manager move-in, demolition, government order, HUD sale, hotel conversion, or conversion to affordable housing). Tenants evicted for no-fault reasons are entitled to relocation assistance; those evicted for at-fault reasons are not.
rules.citation: L.A.M.C. (Los Angeles Municipal Code) – Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance
rules.quotedSpan: Under the JCO, the landlord may recover possession of a rental unit in specific situations... These reasons include The owner or an immediate family member will move into the rental unit; Resident manager will move into the rental unit when required by law or by an affordable housing covenant or regulatory agreement; Demolition, permanent removal from the rental market, or conversion to non-residential; Government order to vacate; HUD owns and is selling the property; Residential Hotel being converted or demolished; Conversion to affordable housing.
rules.coverageDescription: Applies to most residential rental properties in Los Angeles not regulated by RSO. Covers buildings newer than October 1, 1978. Does not apply to: transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternities/sororities, owner's roommate situations, some cooperatives, nonprofit homeless facilities, short-term substance abuse treatment centers, HACLA-owned or government properties, and single-family homes/condos owned by natural persons (without corporate/REIT/LLC ownership) where the owner occupied the unit and notified the tenant in writing of the exemption. Applies to single-family dwellings when only one unit exists on the lot.
exemptions: Properties owned by HACLA or government

Single-family homes and condos owned by natural persons if owner-occupied and tenant was notified in writing (does not apply if multiple units on same lot or second residential unit cannot be sold separately)
warnings: Source does not provide an exact enactment date or effective date for JCO; effective date status inferred from document date and context indicating ordinance is in force
Coverage rules for single-family homes complex; exemption requires both ownership and notification criteria
Source references but does not fully detail the RSO (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)

rules.title: Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance – Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Evictions
rules.requirement: Property owners must pay relocation assistance to tenants when evicting them for no-fault reasons (owner/family move-in, manager move-in, demolition, government order, HUD sale, hotel conversion, or conversion to affordable housing). No relocation assistance is required if the tenant is at fault for the eviction.
rules.citation: L.A.M.C. – Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance
rules.quotedSpan: Situations in which the property owner wishes to regain the use of the rental unit, as the result of a personal or business decision, and not the tenant's fault, may be cause for eviction, but the property owner may have to pay the tenant relocation assistance.
exemptions: Evictions for at-fault reasons (failure to pay rent, lease violation, nuisance, illegal use, failure to renew, denial of access, unapproved subtenant)
warnings: Source does not specify the amount or formula for relocation assistance; only states it may be required
Exact relocation assistance amounts would be in separate regulation or LAHD guidelines not quoted here

rules.title: Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance – Tenancy Duration and Application Requirements
rules.requirement: JCO protections apply only if the tenant has lived in the same unit for at least six months or their original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
rules.citation: L.A.M.C. – Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance
rules.quotedSpan: In order to apply to a tenancy, it requires that the tenant either has lived in the same unit for at least six months or that their original lease expired, whichever comes first.
rules.coverageDescription: Same jurisdiction and building coverage as JCO generally, but applies only to tenancies meeting the six-month or lease-expiration threshold.
exemptions: Tenancies shorter than six months where the original lease has not yet expired
warnings: This is a threshold rule affecting when JCO protections apply, not an additional eviction category

rules.title: Evictions for Non-Payment of Rent – Fair Market Rent Threshold
rules.effectiveDateQuote: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).
rules.requirement: Landlords may not evict a tenant for non-payment of rent unless the amount of rent owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent (FMR) for the unit's bedroom size. FMR thresholds vary by bedroom count.
rules.citation: L.A.M.C. – Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (Non-Payment of Rent)
rules.quotedSpan: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR). The FMR depends on the bedroom size of the rental unit.
rules.coverageDescription: Applies to all RSO and JCO rental units in Los Angeles.
warnings: Source states FMR depends on bedroom size but does not provide specific FMR dollar amounts; those amounts are referenced as external data
The source gives only one example (1-bedroom at $1,500 rent) and notes it is below FMR, but exact FMR figures not provided in this document
Document does not state the effective date of the main JCO ordinance itself; only March 27, 2023 is given for the non-payment rule
Document does not provide dollar amounts for relocation assistance or the complete FMR thresholds by bedroom
Document references AB 1482 (state rent increase law) but that is not in the JCO; see separate rules for state law
August 20, 2025 notice-of-right-to-counsel requirement is mentioned but is procedural, not a substantive eviction rule
Document notes JCO does not regulate rent increases; state law AB 1482 applies separately to buildings over 15 years old
